sources.entry: Accent - Developer-oriented translation tool. (Source Code) BSD-3-Clause Elixir/Docker

summary.one_liner: Accent is a developer-oriented translation tool for managing translations in web and native apps, with a web UI, CLI, collaboration features, and a GraphQL API.
summary.what_it_does: Accent provides a workflow for maintaining translations in web and native apps, with asynchronous collaboration between translators and developers. It keeps a full history of changes, showing who changed what and when, and supports rolling back actions. It includes a web UI for translators and developers, a command line tool for adding Accent to a developer workflow, and threaded discussions around translations. The API that powers the UI is GraphQL, documented and open, so plugins, CLIs, or libraries can be built on it. The README describes a Phoenix/Elixir backend with a PostgreSQL database and a webapp built with Node.js.
use_cases: track who changed which translation and roll back
build a plugin or CLI on top of a translation API
run a self-hosted translation management instance
collaborate with translators on strings in web or native apps
how_to_run: Create a .env file with DATABASE_URL, DUMMY_LOGIN_ENABLED, and SECRET_KEY_BASE (64-byte string, e.g. from openssl rand -hex 64)
Development: install Erlang ~> 26.1, Elixir ~> 1.15, PostgreSQL >= 9.4, Node.js >= 16.19
Run make dependencies, then mix ecto.setup, then mix phx.server
Production-style: run make build, make dev-start-postgresql, make dev-start-application with docker-compose
notable: Full history control with rollback of actions and attribution of who changed what and when
GraphQL API that powers the UI is open and documented
Ships with OpenTelemetry instrumentation exporting traces via OTLP
Many login providers via Ueberauth, including OIDC, GitHub, GitLab, Google, Slack, Discord, and Microsoft
Configuration via environment variables following the Twelve-Factor pattern
caveats: Production use needs a valid authentication setup and proper secret keys; defaults are marked unsafe
The README's Kubernetes helm chart section points to a fork by a third party rather than this repository
keywords: translate app strings with my team
